cards.title: Official LiteLLM docs: native enterprise coverage
items: IDENTITY + OFFBOARDING — Entra/OIDC JWT auth, SCIM provisioning, and JWT-to-virtual-key mapping are native enterprise features. SCIM deprovisioning blocks the user’s virtual keys and clears auth cache; separate GitHub connection cleanup may still be required.

KEYS + MODELS — virtual keys support expiry, model access, budgets and rate limits; model mappings/access groups and token/API clients remain available. Model catalog and non-interactive access are not lost.

GITHUB COPILOT — per-user OAuth requires the same LiteLLM user, stores the GitHub token encrypted in the DB, supports disconnect, GHE.com hosts and model mappings, and shows the connected GitHub username.
CLAUDE + AUDIT — enterprise audit/request logs, beta CLI SSO, OS keychain, lite claude and Claude apiKeyHelper configuration are documented. Claude Desktop-specific automation is not documented.

cards.title: Residual CCGC controls — retain only when policy requires
items: CCGC DIFFERENTIATOR — enforced Entra employee → expected GitHub login and immutable account-ID match during enrollment. LiteLLM documents the connected username, not expected-account enforcement; a GHE.com host narrows the risk.
CCGC DIFFERENTIATOR — custom attempt-bounded and binding/catalog-revision-bound admission grants, including stale-admission invalidation beyond native key or JWT expiration.
CCGC DIFFERENTIATOR — exact end-to-end correlation across Entra identity, GitHub connection, custom admission, model and request, beyond native admin audit and request logs.
CCGC DIFFERENTIATOR — managed Claude Desktop-specific installation and conflict recovery where policy requires it. Lite CLI substantially covers Claude Code, but CLI SSO is beta.
